_comment: The Journey Library's authored templates, keyed by template id. THIS FILE IS THE TRANSLATION CACHE (D55): content is authored in English — the experts' language — and each template is rendered once per language and stored here, so a Hebrew or Spanish user reads their own language with no model call, no cost and no network. {ACTION} is the user's own words and is inserted AFTER this lookup; it must never be translated.

anchor.essence: Attach it to something you already do every day.
anchor.pick: Pick something you already do every day, and decide to do {ACTION} right after it
anchor.rehearse: Do {ACTION} straight after that thing once, just to see how it fits

tiny.essence: Start smaller than feels worth it, then grow from there.
tiny.define: Decide the smallest version of {ACTION} that you could not fail to do
tiny.first: Do that smallest version of {ACTION} today

prepare.essence: Do most of the work in advance, so the moment itself needs no decision.
prepare.gather: Get everything {ACTION} needs, and put it where you will see it
prepare.place: Set up the spot where {ACTION} is going to happen

friction.question: When you have tried to keep something up before, what usually got in the way?
friction.noOccasion: It never found a place in my day.
friction.tooBig: I took on more than I could keep up.
friction.deciding: Having to decide each time was the hard part.

nextStep.goal: Understand what my next step in my career is

axis.question: When you are weighing up a direction, what helps you more: understanding it first, or trying it and seeing?
axis.clarityFirst: Understand it first, and only then try.
axis.actionFirst: Try something small, and learn from it.
axis.both: A little clarity, then straight out into the real world.

clarityFirst.essence: Build the criteria and the candidate directions first, and only then take them to the real world.
clarityFirst.m0: I know what my next direction has to give me, and what it has to respect
clarityFirst.m1: I have two plausible directions worth testing
clarityFirst.m2: I have compared both directions against real-world information
clarityFirst.m3: I have tested the leading direction through a small piece of real work
clarityFirst.m4: I have chosen my next move and started it

s0.title: Pick one task at work that gives you energy and one that drains you
s0.description: Two real examples from the past month are enough. Start from your own experience, not from job titles.

s1.title: Turn those two examples into three criteria and two constraints
s1.description: For example: the kind of problems, learning, working across teams, income stability, or a limit on time for studying.

s2.title: Choose two plausible directions that seem to fit those criteria
s2.description: These are hypotheses to test, not a decision. Do not sign up for a course and do not commit to a direction yet.

s3.title: Look through a small sample of current roles in the first direction
s3.description: Check what repeats across the roles, what attracts you, what puts you off, and what is still unclear.

s4.title: Do the same check for the second direction
s4.description: Use the same criteria, so you are not choosing by job title alone.

s5.title: Talk to one person who knows the direction that looks strongest right now
s5.description: Come with two or three questions about the actual work, the hard parts, and what surprises people who enter the field.

s6.title: Map one problem you already know that resembles the work in the leading direction
s6.description: For example: a problem that keeps coming back for customers, who it affects, and what you think causes it.

s7.title: Write a short improvement proposal for the problem you mapped
s7.description: This is a cheap, reversible experiment that simulates part of the work without a long course.

s8.title: Choose your next career move from the evidence you gathered
s8.description: For example: one more piece of proof, a defined skill gap, a focused search, or testing one more direction.

s9.title: Take the first action of the move you chose
s9.description: Start the move with one real action.

actionFirst.essence: Start with one small experiment inside work you already know, and let it narrow the directions.
actionFirst.m0: I have tried a small piece of work built on what already gives me energy
actionFirst.m1: I have turned what I learned into two plausible directions
actionFirst.m2: I have checked whether those directions really contain the work I am looking for
actionFirst.m3: I know what my next direction has to give me, and what it has to respect
actionFirst.m4: I have chosen my next move and started it

s0.title: Pick one problem that keeps coming back at work and that you would like to solve differently
s0.description: Choose a problem you already know. You do not need to know which job title it "belongs" to yet.

s1.title: Map briefly who the problem affects and what seems to cause it
s1.description: The aim is to have material for an experiment, not a perfect document.

s2.title: Write a short improvement proposal, or another way of handling the problem
s2.description: This is a first experiment, and it produces information about which kind of work gives you energy.

s3.title: Write down what in the experiment gave you energy and what did not
s3.description: Focus on what you actually did: analysing, coordinating, writing, solving a problem, working with people.

s4.title: Turn what you learned into two plausible career directions
s4.description: The coach can suggest possibilities, but they stay hypotheses to test.

s5.title: Look through a small sample of current roles in both directions
s5.description: Look for the overlap between what you enjoyed in the experiment and what the roles actually ask for.

s6.title: Talk to one person who knows the leading direction
s6.description: Ask whether the kind of work you tried really appears in the role, and what it looks like day to day.

s7.title: Write three criteria and two constraints for the final choice
s7.description: By now the criteria rest on something you have done, not only on a guess.

s8.title: Choose your next career move from the evidence you gathered
s8.description: Choose one move, not a career for life.

s9.title: Take the first action of the move you chose
s9.description: Start for real: a piece of proof, a conversation, a defined skill gap, or a focused search.

hybrid.essence: A little clarity, then a fast real-world test, and narrowing only from what it taught you.
hybrid.m0: I have one hypothesis good enough to test without committing to it
hybrid.m1: I have tested that hypothesis both in information and in a small action
hybrid.m2: I know what got stronger, what got weaker, and what I still need to find out
hybrid.m3: I have closed the last information gap that was blocking a decision
hybrid.m4: I have chosen my next move and started it

s0.title: Write in one sentence what you want more of in your next job, and what you want less of
s0.description: No long list. One sentence, based on how the work feels to you today.

s1.title: Choose one direction that looks plausible enough to test right now
s1.description: This is a temporary hypothesis. You do not have to be sure.

s2.title: Read two current role descriptions in that direction
s2.description: Look for three things only: what attracts you, what puts you off, and what is still unclear.

s3.title: Run one micro-experiment that simulates part of the work in that direction
s3.description: Choose a small, cheap action you can do out of the experience you already have.

s4.title: Write down what became clearer after the reading and the experiment
s4.description: What got stronger, what is off the table, and what still needs checking.

s5.title: Add a second direction only if real doubt is left
s5.description: If the first direction looks promising enough, there is no need to add an option just to have something to compare against.

s6.title: Talk to one person who knows the direction that is leading now
s6.description: Use the conversation to close the gaps you have left, not to start the research over.

s7.title: Write three criteria and two constraints for the decision
s7.description: Build them out of what you have already learned, not before any contact with reality.

s8.title: Choose your next career move
s8.description: Choose the most reasonable next step, not a career for life.

s9.title: Take the first action of the move you chose
s9.description: Move from a decision to something you actually did.

twoOptions.goal: Decide between two concrete career options

axis.question: When you settle between two options, what convinces you in the end?
axis.criteria: Clear criteria and an orderly comparison.
axis.experience: Trying each one and seeing how it feels.
axis.people: Hearing it from people who actually live it.

criteriaFirst.essence: Decide what matters first, measure both options by it, and close only the gaps that could change the answer.
criteriaFirst.m0: I know what I am really choosing by
criteriaFirst.m1: I have compared both options on the same measuring stick
criteriaFirst.m2: I have closed the main information gap that was blocking the decision
criteriaFirst.m3: I have chosen an option and started the next move

s0.title: Write three things the choice has to give you and two it has to respect
s0.description: Use what you have already said matters to you. Do not build a list of ten criteria.

s1.title: Define what would count as a strong sign for each of those criteria
s1.description: For example: if working across teams matters, what would you expect to see in the role itself?

s2.title: Check the first option against those criteria
s2.description: Use current information about real roles, and write down: evidence for, evidence against, and what is still unknown.

s3.title: Check the second option against exactly the same criteria
s3.description: Use the same criteria, so the comparison is a fair one.

s4.title: Pick the two unknowns that could genuinely change the decision
s4.description: Do not research everything that interests you. Only what would change your choice if the answer came back different.

s5.title: Close one of them through a conversation or a reliable source
s5.description: Choose the shortest route to real evidence on the most important question.

s6.title: Choose the option that wins on your evidence and your constraints
s6.description: If neither wins, name one last unknown and stop there. The aim is a good enough decision, not certainty.

s7.title: Take a first step in the direction you chose
s7.description: A follow-up conversation, a small piece of proof, or checking one skill gap. Keep it cheap and reversible.

testFirst.essence: Live a short piece of each option before deciding, then check the winner against your constraints.
testFirst.m0: I have lived a small piece of each of the two options
testFirst.m1: I know which one felt more like me, and which less
testFirst.m2: I have checked that the leading option also fits my constraints
testFirst.m3: I have chosen an option and started the next move

s0.title: Choose a small task that simulates part of the first option
s0.description: Something you can do with material already available to you: no course, and no asking to change roles.

s1.title: Run that micro-experiment for the first option
s1.description: The point is to feel the kind of work — analysing, coordinating, improving something — not to prove you are already good at it.

s2.title: Choose a small task that simulates part of the second option
s2.description: Keep it about the same size in time and effort, so the comparison is not tilted.

s3.title: Run that micro-experiment for the second option
s3.description: Test the kind of work itself, not only whether the result came out well.

s4.title: Write what each experiment gave you, what took too much out of you, and what you would do again
s4.description: Use the experience as evidence, not as a single gut feeling.

s5.title: Check two critical constraints against both options
s5.description: For example pay or stability, or something the role must include. Use current information where you need it.

s6.title: Choose the option with the better combination of fit and constraints right now
s6.description: If doubt is left, write one single question that could turn the decision around.

s7.title: Take a first step in the direction you chose
s7.description: Start something small and reversible that goes deeper: a piece of proof, a conversation, or mapping a gap.

conversationFirst.essence: Learn from people inside both options, verify what you heard, and test the choice before committing.
conversationFirst.m0: I have heard what both options actually look like
conversationFirst.m1: I have verified the differences that matter to me against other evidence
conversationFirst.m2: I have chosen an option and tested it before committing
conversationFirst.m3: I have started the next move in the direction I chose

s0.title: Write two questions you would ask someone who lives one of these options day to day
s0.description: Questions about the actual work: what eats the time, what is hard, and what people outside it do not understand.

s1.title: Have one reality conversation with someone who knows the first option
s1.description: The aim is to understand the work, not to ask for a job or to impress anyone.

s2.title: Have one reality conversation with someone who knows the second option
s2.description: Use the same two base questions, so you can actually compare the answers.

s3.title: Write down three meaningful differences you heard between the options
s3.description: Focus on what affects your own fit: the kind of problems, the collaboration, the pace, the stability, the learning.

s4.title: Check against current information whether the two most important things you heard show up in real roles
s4.description: A conversation is evidence, not the whole truth. Look for corroboration.

s5.title: Choose the option that fits better right now, and say why
s5.description: Write the decision in one sentence, including the trade-off you are willing to accept.

s6.title: Run one small reality check on the option you chose
s6.description: Before any big commitment, do one small thing that makes sure the decision does not rest on a conversation alone.

s7.title: Start the next career move in the direction you chose
s7.description: Choose a reversible step: a piece of proof, a focused skill gap, or a follow-up conversation.

fitTest.goal: Check whether a direction that interests me really fits, before committing to it

axis.question: How would you rather test whether a direction suits you?
axis.work: Doing a small piece of the work myself.
axis.people: Talking to people who live it.
axis.realContext: Doing a small task for a real need.

workSample.essence: Do a small piece of the work itself, and tell a skill gap apart from a bad fit.
workSample.m0: I have lived a small stretch of work like the direction that interests me
workSample.m1: I know what drew me in and what did not
workSample.m2: I have compared my experience with what real roles actually involve
workSample.m3: I have decided whether to go deeper, and taken the next step

s0.title: Choose one small question from work or from life that this kind of work could answer
s0.description: Choose a question that genuinely interests you. It does not need to be an impressive project.

s1.title: Find the smallest material you need to answer it
s1.description: Use what you are already allowed to work with, or what is public. Do not let the search become a project of its own.

s2.title: Do the small piece of work that tries to answer the question
s2.description: The aim is to live the sequence — understand a question, work through it, reach a conclusion, say it clearly — not to meet a professional standard.

s3.title: Write three lines: what you enjoyed, what drained you, and what you would be willing to learn
s3.description: Separate "I do not know how yet" from "I do not like this kind of work".

s4.title: Read two current role descriptions in the direction you are testing
s4.description: Look for whether the kind of work you just did appears in real roles, and what is still missing from the picture.

s5.title: Decide whether to go deeper, to stop, or to run one more check
s5.description: Choose by fit, not by how well the first attempt went.

s6.title: Take a small step in line with that decision
s6.description: Going deeper: pick one skill or piece of proof to build. Stopping: write down what you learned about what to look for next.

conversation.essence: Learn it from two people who live the work, then feel the one part you cannot take on trust.
conversation.m0: I have heard what the work looks like from two real points of view
conversation.m1: I have verified what actually repeats in real roles, not just in one conversation
conversation.m2: I have felt for myself the one part that mattered most to test
conversation.m3: I have decided whether to go deeper in this direction

s0.title: Write three questions that would show you what the work is like day to day
s0.description: Ask about the kind of tasks, the draining parts, and what surprises people who move into it.

s1.title: Talk to one person doing this work about a real working day
s1.description: The aim is to understand the work, not to be told whether you should switch.

s2.title: Talk to one more person, in a different setting or at a different level of experience
s2.description: The second conversation is what stops one person’s experience from becoming the truth about a whole profession.

s3.title: Write down three things that came up in both conversations, and one that differed
s3.description: Look for patterns in the work itself, not only for career advice.

s4.title: Check two current role descriptions against what you heard
s4.description: Verify that the main tasks they described also show up in the roles that are actually out there.

s5.title: Choose the one part of the work you still need to feel for yourself
s5.description: A conversation can teach a great deal, but it cannot fully replace doing it.

s6.title: Run a micro-test of the part you chose
s6.description: A short piece of work that lets you feel the kind of work without committing to any training.

s7.title: Decide whether to go deeper, to stop, or to look at another direction
s7.description: Sum up the decision from what the people, the market and your own micro-test told you.

realContext.essence: Do one small real task for someone who needs the answer, and test the context as well as the work.
realContext.m0: I have worked on a small question with a real need behind it
realContext.m1: I got feedback, and I know how the real context felt
realContext.m2: I have checked how much of that experience represents the wider role
realContext.m3: I have decided whether to go deeper, and taken the next step

s0.title: Find one small real problem where this kind of work would help someone decide something
s0.description: Best from a context already open to you: work, a personal project, a community. Do not invent a large project.

s1.title: Agree with that person, or that context, on the question you are answering
s1.description: Keep the scope small: one question, not a whole system.

s2.title: Do the small piece of work and give back an answer they can use
s2.description: The aim is to feel what it is like to work with real context and real responsibility to someone, not to build a perfect portfolio.

s3.title: Ask for one piece of feedback on what was useful and what was missing
s3.description: This is feedback on the work, not a grade on whether the career suits you.

s4.title: Write down what changed when the work was for a real need rather than an exercise
s4.description: Check whether you enjoyed clarifying the question, doing the work, explaining it, and the back-and-forth around the result.

s5.title: Read two current role descriptions to see how much of this represents the direction
s5.description: Separate this particular experience from the wider role.

s6.title: Decide whether to go deeper, to stop, or to test one more part
s6.description: Choose on fit, not on one successful attempt.

s7.title: Take a small step in line with that decision
s7.description: Going deeper: choose one focused skill or piece of proof. If not: write down what you learned about the kind of work you do want.

jobTarget.goal: Find a new job when it is not yet clear which roles to aim at

axis.question: Where would you rather start narrowing the search from?
axis.criteria: From what I want in my next role.
axis.market: From the openings themselves, and what repeats in them.
axis.people: From people who know the market.

criteriaFirst.essence: Say what the next role has to give you, and narrow the market down to it.
criteriaFirst.m0: I know what I am looking for in my next role
criteriaFirst.m1: I have narrowed it down to two plausible targets
criteriaFirst.m2: I have chosen a main target and a backup
criteriaFirst.m3: I have started a focused search for the main target

s0.title: Pick two tasks from your current work you would want more of, and less of
s0.description: Real examples from the past month are enough.

s1.title: Turn those examples into three criteria for the next role
s1.description: For example: the kind of problems, working with people, depth of analysis, or how much is yours to own.

s2.title: Choose no more than three possible target roles

s3.title: Compare a small sample of openings from each target against those criteria
s3.description: Look for patterns, not for one perfect opening.

s4.title: Drop the one target that does not hold up well enough against them
s4.description: Write down why it is going.

s5.title: Choose a main target and a backup
s5.description: The main target has to be clear enough to focus a search around.

s6.title: Take one search action for the main target only
s6.description: For example a focused search, or adjusting how you show the evidence for it.

postingsFirst.essence: Start from the roles that already appeal to you, and read the pattern in them.
postingsFirst.m0: I can see what repeats in the roles that attract me
postingsFirst.m1: I have narrowed the market to two families of roles
postingsFirst.m2: I have chosen a clear search target
postingsFirst.m3: I have tested that target through a focused search

s0.title: Collect five openings that made you stop and think "this is interesting"
s0.description: Even if the job titles are completely different from one another.

s1.title: Mark what repeats across those five
s1.description: Look for tasks, problems and working environments that come up more than once.

s2.title: Group them into two families of roles
s2.description: Group by the actual work, not by the job title.

s3.title: Check three more openings from each family

s4.title: Choose the family that fits your experience and your constraints better
s4.description: This is choosing a search target, not a professional identity.

s5.title: Write your search target as one sentence
s5.description: A sentence that names the role, the kind of work, and the kind of place.

s6.title: Run one focused search using that new sentence
s6.description: Check whether the results come back more relevant than before.

conversationFirst.essence: Get two realistic directions from people who know the market, then verify them against real openings.
conversationFirst.m0: I have two realistic directions out of real conversations
conversationFirst.m1: I have verified that those directions exist and suit me in the market
conversationFirst.m2: I have chosen a main target
conversationFirst.m3: I have started a focused search for it

s0.title: Choose two people who can show you roles close to what you already do
s0.description: Ideally people who see several functions, not only their own.

s1.title: Have one conversation aimed at naming two or three realistic directions
s1.description: Ask for examples of roles, not for advice about your career.

s2.title: Have a second conversation and see whether the same directions come up
s2.description: The second conversation is what verifies the first.

s3.title: Check a small sample of openings in the two directions that repeated
s3.description: Look for whether the actual work matches what you were told.

s4.title: Choose a main target on fit, experience and constraints
s4.description: Keep the second one as a backup only.

s5.title: Take a first search action for the main target
s5.description: For example one more focused conversation, or adjusting how you show the evidence for it.

proof.goal: Present my experience so that more of my applications get an answer

axis.question: Where should the proof that you fit come from?
axis.existing: From the experience I already have.
axis.build: Building something small that shows the capability.
axis.story: Telling what I have already done differently.

extractExisting.essence: Turn experience you already have into clear proof, without inventing anything.
extractExisting.m0: I have mapped real experience of mine onto what the target asks for
extractExisting.m1: I have written proof that is clear and believable
extractExisting.m2: That proof is now part of how I present myself
extractExisting.m3: I have tried the new version in a real search action

s0.title: Choose one target opening that represents well what you are looking for
s0.description: It will serve as your reference point.

s1.title: Mark three central requirements you can already prove

s2.title: For each requirement, find one real example from your past
s2.description: Write the situation, what you did, and what it changed.

s3.title: Turn two of those examples into short lines of proof
s3.description: Without inflating anything and without inventing anything.

s4.title: Put the proof into the document or profile that matters
s4.description: Update only what actually affects this target.

s5.title: Use the new version in one real search action
s5.description: An application, an approach, or sharing it with someone.

buildArtifact.essence: Make one small thing that shows the capability your existing experience cannot show.
buildArtifact.m0: I have chosen the one gap in my proof worth closing
buildArtifact.m1: I have made something that shows the capability
buildArtifact.m2: I have checked that it is understood and relevant
buildArtifact.m3: I have used it in a real search action

s0.title: Choose one requirement that keeps appearing in your target roles and is hard for you to prove today
s0.description: Choose a gap in the PROOF, not a skill you do not have.

s1.title: Define one small thing you could make that would show that capability
s1.description: For example a map of a process, or a short piece of analysis.

s2.title: Build a first version of it
s2.description: Use only material you are allowed to show.

s3.title: Check whether someone who knows this work understands what it proves
s3.description: Ask them about relevance, not about how it looks.

s4.title: Improve it once, from what they told you
s4.description: The aim is proof that is good enough to use, not a finished product.

s5.title: Fold it into how you present yourself
s5.description: Tie it explicitly to the requirement it proves.

s6.title: Use it in one real search action
s6.description: See whether explaining why you fit has become easier.

roleStory.essence: Tell what you have already done in the language of value the target role is looking for.
roleStory.m0: I have connected my experience to the value the target is looking for
roleStory.m1: I have built proof stories that hold up
roleStory.m2: I have checked that they convey the right capability
roleStory.m3: I have used them in a real search action

s0.title: Choose a target opening and mark three kinds of value it is looking for
s0.description: For example: owning something end to end, coordinating between people, or improving how work gets done.

s1.title: Choose three past experiences that show that value
s1.description: They do not have to come from the same job title.

s2.title: Write each one as a short story: the problem, what you did, what changed
s2.description: If you do not have an exact number, do not invent one.

s3.title: Turn one story into a written version and a spoken one
s3.description: The same evidence, in two forms: one for the page, one for a conversation.

s4.title: Check with one person what they think the story proves
s4.description: Ask them to describe the capability they heard, in their own words.

s5.title: Update the other two stories in the same way

s6.title: Use one of the stories in a real search action
s6.description: An application, an approach, or preparing for an interview.

access.goal: Reach more relevant opportunities and people in my job search

axis.question: Which route to people feels possible for you right now?
axis.warm: Through people who already know me.
axis.community: Through a professional place I keep coming back to.
axis.targeted: A focused approach to someone I have a reason to talk to.

warmNetwork.essence: Use the ties you already have, naturally and with a clear reason.
warmNetwork.m0: I have found the existing ties that could open information or a way in
warmNetwork.m1: I have made two natural, focused approaches
warmNetwork.m2: I have turned a reply into information, a conversation or an introduction
warmNetwork.m3: I have a way of using this route again

s0.title: List five people who already know you and might be one connection away from the field
s0.description: They do not need to be important people.

s1.title: Choose the two you have a natural reason to contact
s1.description: Ask for a perspective or an introduction, not for a job.

s2.title: Send one approach that says clearly why you are writing
s2.description: Write what you are asking about and what would actually help.

s3.title: Send the second one
s3.description: Improve the wording first if the first one taught you something.

s4.title: Follow through on whatever conversation or introduction came out of it
s4.description: Write down what you learned and what the next step is.

s5.title: Choose one way to use this route once a week

repeatedCommunity.essence: Trade one-off networking for turning up again where connections form on their own.
repeatedCommunity.m0: I have found a relevant community and seen how it works
repeatedCommunity.m1: I have taken part in it more than once
repeatedCommunity.m2: One professional connection has formed naturally
repeatedCommunity.m3: I have decided whether this becomes a route I keep using

s0.title: Choose one professional community where people from the field keep meeting
s0.description: Somewhere that comes round again is better than a one-off event.

s1.title: Turn up once, just to understand what happens there
s1.description: Notice who takes part and how connections actually form.

s2.title: Next time, contribute one small thing
s2.description: A good question, an answer to someone, or one short conversation.

s3.title: Come back to the same community one more time
s3.description: The point is that people start recognising you.

s4.title: Open one conversation with the person the contact came most naturally with
s4.description: Ask about the work, out of the context you already share.

s5.title: Decide whether this community is worth keeping as a route
s5.description: If it is, set the minimum you will keep up.

targetedConversations.essence: Small, precise approaches to specific people who hold something worth knowing.
targetedConversations.m0: I have found specific people I have a real reason to talk to
targetedConversations.m1: I have sent focused approaches rather than generic ones
targetedConversations.m2: I have turned a reply into information, a conversation or a connection
targetedConversations.m3: I have set a small pace I can actually repeat

s0.title: Choose three companies or teams you would like to understand better
s0.description: Choose places that are relevant to your target.

s1.title: In each one, find a person who could tell you something useful
s1.description: It does not have to be a recruiter.

s2.title: Write one specific question for each of them
s2.description: Why this person in particular, and what you want to understand.

s3.title: Send two focused approaches
s3.description: Ask for a short perspective, not for a job.

s4.title: If someone replies, have a short conversation and take away one insight and one next step
s4.description: If nobody replies, learn from the wording and try the third person.

s5.title: Send one follow-up that continues the contact naturally
s5.description: A thank you with a short update, or the question that came out of the conversation.

s6.title: Decide whether this route is worth repeating weekly
s6.description: For example two good approaches a week.
